title: Cognitive Set 02: Arithmetic & Analytical Depth
description: High-yield quant, cloud-spend DI, linear seating, blood relations, syllogisms, and editorial verbal drills.

questions.question: A is 50% more efficient than B. Working together, A and B can complete a software migration in 12 days. If A works alone for 6 days and then leaves, how many days will B take alone to finish the remaining work?
questions.explanation: Let B's rate = 2 units/day, so A's rate = 3 units/day. Combined rate = 5 units/day, giving total work = 5 * 12 = 60 units. In 6 days, A finishes 6 * 3 = 18 units. Remaining work = 60 - 18 = 42 units. Time for B = 42 / 2 = 21 days.
questions.shortcut: Total work = (3+2)*12 = 60 units; subtract 6*3 = 18 => 42/2 = 21 days.

questions.question: What is the remainder when 17^203 is divided by 18?
questions.shortcut: 17 = 18 - 1; (-1)^odd = -1, which corresponds to remainder 18 - 1 = 17.

questions.question: Four years ago, the average age of a 5-member project team was 28 years. Today, a new engineer joined the team, making the current average age of all 6 members 30 years. What is the present age of the new engineer?
questions.explanation: Four years ago, sum of 5 members = 5 * 28 = 140 years. Today, each of those 5 is 4 years older, so their combined age is 140 + 20 = 160 years. Current sum of 6 members = 6 * 30 = 180 years. New engineer's age = 180 - 160 = 20 years.
questions.shortcut: Current sum of original 5 = 5*(28+4) = 160; 6*30 - 160 = 20.

questions.question: A solid metallic cylinder of radius 6 cm and height 15 cm is melted and recast into identical solid cones each of radius 3 cm and height 5 cm. Assuming zero wastage, how many cones are formed?
questions.explanation: Volume of cylinder = pi * 6^2 * 15 = 540*pi cm^3. Volume of one cone = (1/3) * pi * 3^2 * 5 = 15*pi cm^3. Number of cones = 540*pi / (15*pi) = 36.

questions.question: P starts a venture with Rs. 45,000. Four months later, Q joins with Rs. 60,000, and six months after the start, R joins with Rs. 90,000. At the end of one year, they earn a total profit of Rs. 52,000. What is Q's share of the profit?
Two fair six-sided dice are rolled simultaneously. What is the probability that the sum of the two numbers appearing is a prime number strictly greater than 5?
questions.explanation: Possible sums from 2 to 12 that are prime and > 5 are 7 and 11. Pairs summing to 7: (1,6),(2,5),(3,4),(4,3),(5,2),(6,1) = 6 pairs. Pairs summing to 11: (5,6),(6,5) = 2 pairs. Total favorable = 8 out of 36 => 8/36 = 2/9.
questions.shortcut: Primes in [6,12] are 7 (6 ways) and 11 (2 ways) => 8/36 = 2/9.

questions.question: Alloy A contains copper and zinc in the ratio 5 : 3, while Alloy B contains copper and zinc in the ratio 7 : 5. In what ratio must Alloy A and Alloy B be melted together to obtain a new alloy with copper and zinc in the ratio 11 : 7?
questions.shortcut: Convert copper fractions to denominator 72: A=45, B=42, Target=44 => ratio (44-42):(45-44) = 2:1.

questions.question: Solve for real x > 2: log_3(x - 2) + log_3(x + 6) = 2
questions.explanation: Combine logarithms: log_3((x - 2)(x + 6)) = 2 => (x - 2)(x + 6) = 3^2 = 9. Expanding gives x^2 + 4x - 12 = 9 => x^2 + 4x - 21 = 0 => (x + 7)(x - 3) = 0. Since x > 2, x = 3.
questions.shortcut: Test x=3: (3-2)(3+6) = 1*9 = 9 = 3^2 immediately.

questions.passage:
Quarterly Cloud Infrastructure Spend (in Rs Lakhs):
- Q1: Compute 40, Storage 25, Network 15 (Total 80)
- Q2: Compute 50, Storage 30, Network 20 (Total 100)
- Q3: Compute 60, Storage 35, Network 25 (Total 120)
- Q4: Compute 100, Storage 60, Network 40 (Total 200)
questions.question: From the Quarterly Cloud Spend table, what percentage of the total annual cloud spend across all four quarters was spent on Compute?
questions.explanation: Total Compute spend = 40 + 50 + 60 + 100 = 250 Lakhs. Total annual spend = 80 + 100 + 120 + 200 = 500 Lakhs. Percentage = (250 / 500) * 100 = 50%.
questions.shortcut: Every quarter Compute is 50% of total (40/80, 50/100, 60/120, 100/200), so overall is 50%.

questions.passage:
Quarterly Cloud Infrastructure Spend (in Rs Lakhs):
- Q1: Compute 40, Storage 25, Network 15 (Total 80)
- Q2: Compute 50, Storage 30, Network 20 (Total 100)
- Q3: Compute 60, Storage 35, Network 25 (Total 120)
- Q4: Compute 100, Storage 60, Network 40 (Total 200)
questions.question: What was the percentage increase in Storage spend from Q1 to Q4?
questions.explanation: Storage spend rose from 25 Lakhs in Q1 to 60 Lakhs in Q4. Increase = 60 - 25 = 35 Lakhs. Percentage increase = (35 / 25) * 100 = 140%.

questions.question: Ten analysts sit in two parallel rows of 5 each. Row 1 (A, B, C, D, E) faces South; Row 2 (P, Q, R, S, T) faces North, directly opposite Row 1. B sits at an extreme end, and D sits third to the right of B. The person facing D sits immediately left of R. Q sits second to the left of R. A faces Q. P sits at an extreme end and faces B. E sits directly between D and C. Who sits directly opposite C?
questions.explanation: Index seats 1 to 5 from West to East. Facing South, right is toward seat 1; facing North, right is toward seat 5. B=5 (East end) => D = 5-3 = 2. Person facing D(2) is seat 2 in Row 2, immediately left of R => R=3. Q is 2nd left of R(3) => Q=1. A faces Q => A=1. P faces B(5) => P=5. E sits between D(2) and C => E=3 and C=4. The remaining seat in Row 2 is seat 4 = S, which faces C(4).
questions.shortcut: West-to-East 1..5: Row1 = [A, D, E, C, B], Row2 = [Q, T, R, S, P] => S faces C.

questions.question: Statements: (1) Only a few queries are indexed. (2) All indexed items are cached. (3) No cached item is volatile. Conclusions: I. Some queries are not indexed. II. No indexed item is volatile. III. Some queries are cached.
options: All I, II, and III follow
questions.explanation: 'Only a few queries are indexed' implies both 'some queries are indexed' AND 'some queries are not indexed' (so I follows). Since all indexed items are cached and no cached item is volatile, no indexed item can be volatile (II follows). Finally, the queries that are indexed are also cached (III follows).
questions.shortcut: 'Only a few' always encodes BOTH 'some' and 'some not'.

questions.question: Pointing to a photograph of a woman, Arjun says, 'Her mother's only grandson is my son, and I have no siblings.' How is the woman in the photograph related to Arjun?
questions.explanation: 'Her mother's only grandson' is Arjun's son. Since Arjun has no siblings, Arjun cannot be the woman's brother; the woman's mother's daughter is the woman herself, and her son is Arjun's son. Therefore, the woman in the photograph is Arjun's wife.
questions.shortcut: Arjun has no siblings => the mother of Arjun's son (who is also the woman's mother's daughter) must be Arjun's wife.

questions.question: Identify the single WRONG number in the series: 12, 18, 30, 54, 102, 196, 390
questions.explanation: Differences between consecutive terms double each step: 18-12=6, 30-18=12, 54-30=24, 102-54=48. Next difference should be 96, giving 102 + 96 = 198 (not 196), and then 198 + 192 = 390. Hence 196 is wrong.

questions.question: Is the integer k strictly positive? Statement I: k^3 - 4k = 0. Statement II: k^2 + k > 2.
options: Both statements I and II together are sufficient, while neither alone is
Both statements together are still insufficient
questions.explanation: From Statement I: k(k - 2)(k + 2) = 0 => k in {-2, 0, 2}, insufficient. From Statement II: k^2 + k - 2 > 0 => (k + 2)(k - 1) > 0 => k < -2 or k > 1, insufficient. Combining I and II: among {-2, 0, 2}, only k = 2 satisfies k < -2 or k > 1. Thus k = 2 > 0 uniquely.
questions.shortcut: I gives {-2, 0, 2}; II eliminates 0 and -2 (since (-2)^2 + (-2) = 2, not > 2), leaving k=2.

questions.question: In a code language, 'fast cloud deploy' is written as 'ka mi zo', 'secure cloud cluster' is written as 'mi tu re', and 'fast cluster scale' is written as 'zo tu pa'. What is the code for 'deploy scale'?
questions.explanation: 'cloud' appears in statements 1 & 2 => common code 'mi'. 'fast' appears in 1 & 3 => common code 'zo'. Thus in statement 1, 'deploy' = 'ka'. 'cluster' appears in 2 & 3 => 'tu'. Thus in statement 3, 'scale' = 'pa'. Hence 'deploy scale' = 'ka pa'.
questions.shortcut: Eliminate shared words: cloud=mi, fast=zo => deploy=ka; cluster=tu => scale=pa.

questions.question: If 15 August 2024 was a Thursday, what day of the week will 15 August 2029 be?
questions.explanation: From 15 Aug 2024 to 15 Aug 2029 spans 5 years: 2025, 2026, 2027, 2028 (leap year, Feb 29 falls inside), 2029. Odd days = 4 ordinary years (4*1) + 1 leap year (2) = 6 odd days. Thursday + 6 days = Wednesday.
questions.shortcut: 5 years including Feb 2028 = 5 + 1 = 6 odd days => Thursday - 1 day = Wednesday.

questions.question: In a survey of 200 developers, 110 use Git, 95 use Docker, and 85 use Linux. 45 use both Git and Docker, 35 use Docker and Linux, 40 use Git and Linux, and 20 use all three. How many developers use EXACTLY two of these three tools?
questions.explanation: Only(Git & Docker) = 45 - 20 = 25. Only(Docker & Linux) = 35 - 20 = 15. Only(Git & Linux) = 40 - 20 = 20. Total using exactly two = 25 + 15 + 20 = 60.
questions.shortcut: Sum of pairwise intersections minus 3 * (all three) = (45+35+40) - 3*20 = 120 - 60 = 60.

questions.question: One morning after sunrise, Kavya and Rohan stood facing each other in an open courtyard. Kavya noticed that Rohan's shadow fell directly to her own right. Which direction was Rohan facing?
questions.explanation: In the morning, the sun is in the East, so every shadow falls toward the West. Rohan's shadow fell to Kavya's right, meaning Kavya's right is West. Therefore Kavya is facing South. Since they face each other, Rohan is facing North.
questions.shortcut: Morning shadow = West. Kavya's right = West => Kavya faces South => Rohan faces North.

questions.question: Statement: 'To cut cloud egress fees by 30%, our analytics team will compress all nightly Parquet exports using Zstandard before uploading to object storage.' Which assumption is strictly necessary for this plan to achieve the 30% fee cut?
options: Object storage providers bill egress fees primarily based on transferred byte volume rather than flat per-request charges
Zstandard compression runs faster on multi-core CPUs than Gzip
Analysts only query the exported Parquet files during weekday business hours
The company plans to migrate its primary database within six months
questions.explanation: Compressing exports shrinks payload byte size. For smaller payloads to reduce egress fees by 30%, billing must depend directly on byte volume transferred rather than a flat per-request fee.
questions.shortcut: Link mechanism (smaller byte size via compression) to outcome (lower egress bill).

questions.passage: For years, software organizations treated technical documentation as an afterthought—a static wiki updated only during quarterly audits. In distributed engineering teams operating across time zones, however, stale documentation acts as a silent latency tax: new hires spend weeks interrupting senior architects to reconstruct unwritten API contracts. Leading platform teams now treat documentation as code, storing Markdown specifications inside the same version-controlled repositories as application logic and gating pull requests on automated link and schema checks. While this discipline slows initial commit merges slightly, it compresses onboarding timelines and preserves institutional memory when key contributors rotate off a project.
questions.question: What does the author mean by calling stale documentation 'a silent latency tax'?
options: Wiki servers consume excessive network bandwidth across time zones
Outdated docs impose hidden delays on engineering productivity through repeated interruptions
Quarterly compliance audits impose monetary penalties on software vendors
Version-control systems reject pull requests that contain Markdown files
questions.explanation: The passage explains that stale docs cause new hires to spend weeks interrupting senior architects to recover unwritten API contracts—an unmeasured drag on team speed.
questions.shortcut: Check the clause directly after the colon explaining the metaphor.

questions.question: Which trade-off of the 'documentation as code' approach is explicitly acknowledged in the passage?
options: It increases employee turnover among senior architects
It eliminates the need for version-controlled repositories
It adds minor friction to initial pull-request merges
It prevents teams from collaborating across multiple time zones
questions.explanation: The final sentence notes: 'While this discipline slows initial commit merges slightly, it compresses onboarding timelines...'
questions.shortcut: Look for the concession clause starting with 'While this discipline...'.

questions.question: Spot the grammatical error: 'Every intern in the cloud cohort (A) / must submit their security clearance form (B) / before they are granted access (C) / to the staging Kubernetes cluster. (D)'
questions.explanation: In traditional placement grammar tests (AMCAT/Cocubes), singular indefinite phrases like 'Every intern' require singular pronouns ('his or her security clearance form' and 'before he or she is granted') rather than plural 'their'. Note segment (B) introduces the first number mismatch.
questions.shortcut: 'Every + singular noun' takes singular pronouns in formal placement grammar tests.

questions.question:
Order P, Q, R, S into a logical paragraph:
P. Without clear ownership boundaries, shared libraries quickly mutate into dumping grounds for unrelated helper functions.
Q. At that stage, upgrading even a minor utility forces dozens of downstream teams to perform emergency regression testing.
R. Engineering leaders often advocate extracting common code into a single shared package to eliminate duplication.
S. Smart platform teams therefore prefer narrow, single-purpose SDKs over sprawling 'common' packages.
questions.explanation: R introduces the common practice ('single shared package'). P states the pitfall ('shared libraries quickly mutate'). Q describes the consequence ('At that stage'). S gives the takeaway ('therefore prefer narrow SDKs'). Order: R-P-Q-S.
questions.shortcut: 'At that stage' in Q follows P's 'mutate into dumping grounds'; S concludes with 'therefore'.

questions.question: Choose the best correction: 'The compliance auditor insisted that the database administrator [revokes] root credentials immediately.'
questions.explanation: Verbs of demand or urgency ('insisted', 'recommended', 'mandated') followed by 'that' require the mandative subjunctive—the bare infinitive form 'revoke'.
questions.shortcut: Demand verb + that + subject + bare infinitive ('insisted that he revoke').

questions.question: Fill in the blanks: 'Because the outage lasted barely ninety seconds, its financial impact was ______, yet it exposed a ______ flaw in the failover router.'
questions.explanation: A 90-second outage has minimal ('negligible') immediate cost, while 'yet' introduces a serious contrast—a 'critical' flaw in failover.
questions.shortcut: 'Barely ninety seconds' => negligible impact; 'yet' flips to serious => critical flaw.

questions.question: Find the faulty segment: 'Between the two caching engines evaluated, (A) / Redis proved to be the most resilient (B) / under sudden traffic spikes (C) / during load testing. (D)'
questions.explanation: When comparing exactly two items ('Between the two caching engines'), use the comparative degree ('more resilient'), not the superlative ('most resilient').
questions.shortcut: Comparison of 2 entities requires comparative ('more resilient'), not superlative ('most').

questions.question:
Arrange P, Q, R, S logically:
P. This mismatch occurs because CPU speeds have scaled far faster than main memory access latencies.
Q. Modern processors spend a substantial fraction of execution cycles stalled waiting for data from RAM.
R. Multi-level SRAM caches sit close to processor cores precisely to bridge this widening speed gap.
S. Consequently, memory-access patterns often matter more for throughput than raw arithmetic instruction counts.
questions.explanation: Q states the phenomenon (stalled waiting for RAM). P explains 'This mismatch'. R introduces caches to bridge 'this widening speed gap'. S states the practical takeaway ('Consequently'). Order: Q-P-R-S.
questions.shortcut: Q -> P ('This mismatch') -> R ('this widening speed gap') -> S ('Consequently').

questions.question: Select the grammatically accurate option: 'Scarcely had the deployment script finished [than] the health-check endpoint began returning 503 errors.'
questions.explanation: 'Scarcely' and 'Hardly' pair with 'when' (whereas 'No sooner' pairs with 'than').
questions.shortcut: Hardly/Scarcely ... when; No sooner ... than.

questions.question: Claim: 'Our campus placement portal saw a 45% rise in mock-test completions after we added daily streak reminders; therefore, streak reminders directly caused students to practice more.' Which finding most weakens this causal claim?
options: Students who ignored streak reminders were mostly final-year interns already placed
The 45% rise coincided with major IT companies announcing campus recruitment dates two weeks earlier than usual
Mock-test questions were refreshed with updated SQL scenarios during the same quarter
Mobile users accounted for 60% of all portal logins
questions.explanation: If major IT companies announced campus drive dates two weeks earlier right when reminders launched, that external urgency is a strong alternative cause for the surge in mock-test completions.
questions.shortcut: Look for a confounding external trigger (earlier campus drive announcements).
